scenes.text: Start with a real problem. Choose assumptions. Leave out details so the problem becomes manageable. Use equations or a graph to describe the simplified situation. Check whether the answer is reasonable in real life. If it isn't, refine the assumptions and try again. That's the modelling cycle.

scenes.text: A particle ignores dimensions. Size is unimportant here. Smooth means no friction. Rough allows friction, opposing sliding. A rod or beam keeps length and rigid shape. Uniform means evenly spread mass. Weight acts at its centre. Uneven mass shifts it. Light means negligible mass. Omit string weight. A heavy string adds weight. Inextensible means no stretching. Taut over this fixed pulley, it links equal acceleration magnitudes in different directions. A stretching string breaks that link.

beats.text: A box on a desk connects over a pulley to a hanging sphere. Match five simplifications. Ignoring air resistance: which body model is paired here?
Particle. But neglecting air resistance is a separate assumption; a point model can still have drag. Ignore string mass: which word?
Light, because the string's mass is negligible. Same tension on both sides: which pulley?
Smooth pulley, with our light string and ideal pulley. Ignore desk friction: which surface?
Smooth surface: no friction. Same acceleration magnitudes: which string?
Inextensible, while taut, because its fixed length links the movements.
